definition_zh: （利息、款项）累积、自然增长；（权利、利益）产生、归于；积累
definition_en: to increase gradually over time, especially money or interest, or to arise and become due as a right or benefit
core_image: 账本上的数字一点点往上爬，像水慢慢涨过刻度
scene: 老式银行的柜台前，一本存折摊开着，利息按月静静长高。 Interest began to accrue on the deposit after the first month.
sceneCN: 这里 accrue 是「利息逐步累积」（第 1 个义项：利息或款项随时间增长）；句意为存款满一个月后，利息开始累积。

pos.zh: 不及物动词：（利息、利益）累积、增长
及物动词：积累、获得（权利、利益等）

derivatives.zh: 由动词 accrue 加名词后缀 -al 构成，义为「自然增长；应计额」
由动词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「应计的；已累积的」
由动词加 -ment 构成名词，义为「累积的过程」，较少使用

senses.title: Of interest or money: to grow over time
senses.titleCN: 利息或款项随时间增长
senses.definition: to increase as interest or as an amount owed, usually gradually and without any action by the owner
senses.definitionCN: 作为利息或欠款逐步增加，通常不因所有者采取行动而发生
senses.example: Interest accrues on the loan from the day the money is drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款利息从提款当天起开始累积。
senses.why: The Latin root crescere means to grow, and ac- adds the idea of growth toward something, so the amount grows onto the balance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 crescere 意为「生长」，ac- 带「朝向」的意思，于是数额一点点长到账面上。

senses.title: To build up a store of something
senses.definition: to gather or increase gradually, especially benefits, experience, leave, or a store of useful things
senses.definitionCN: 逐步聚拢或增多，尤指益处、经验、假期或有用之物的积累
senses.example: Leave accrued week by week while she stayed on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她留在项目上期间，假期一周周积累起来。
senses.why: A growing amount need not be money: anything that lies unused and adds up follows the same image of steady growth.
senses.whyCN: 增长的不一定是钱：任何闲置而不断加多的东西，都遵循同一个「稳步生长」的画面。

senses.title: Of a right or benefit: to arise and belong
senses.definition: to come into existence as a benefit or right that belongs to someone, often followed by to
senses.definitionCN: 作为属于某人的利益或权利而产生，常后接 to
senses.example: The right to compensation accrued to the workers after the ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 裁决之后，获得赔偿的权利归于工人。
senses.why: A benefit is pictured as growing on the side of its holder, until it stands there fully and belongs to that person.
senses.whyCN: 利益被想象成在其持有者这一侧生长，长成之后便稳稳地属于那个人。

senses.title: To incur a debt or charge
senses.definition: to come to owe money or to become liable for a charge through the passage of time or continued use
senses.definitionCN: 因时间推移或持续使用而欠下款项或承担费用
senses.example: A penalty of five dollars a day accrues if the form is late.
senses.exampleCN: 表格迟交，每天会产生五美元罚金。
senses.why: A debt also grows onto a person: nothing is paid, yet the amount owed keeps rising with each day.
senses.whyCN: 债务同样长在人身上：什么都没付，欠下的数额却随日子一天天升高。

senses.title: Of a fund: to be left to grow
senses.definition: of money or a fund, to be allowed to add up instead of being paid out, so that it grows larger
senses.definitionCN: 指钱或基金不被支出而任其累加，从而变得更多
senses.example: The trust lets income accrue instead of distributing it each year.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托让收益留存累积，而不是每年分配。
senses.why: Here the growth is intentional: the amount is left on the account precisely so that it keeps growing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的增长是有意为之：把数额留在账上，正是为了让它继续生长。

senses.title: To increase in amount or degree
senses.definition: to grow larger or greater in general, as of advantages, costs, pressure, or any measurable quantity
senses.definitionCN: 泛指变大或变多，如优势、成本、压力或任何可衡量的量
senses.example: The advantages of the new system accrued slowly over the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 新系统的优势在头一年里慢慢累积显现。
senses.why: The image of steady upward growth is not tied to money, so it extends to any quantity that builds up.
senses.whyCN: 「稳步上行」的画面并不绑定金钱，因此可延伸到任何逐渐加多的量。

senses.title: In accounting: to record an accrued item
senses.definition: in accounting, to record income or an expense in the period to which it relates, before any cash changes hands
senses.definitionCN: 会计上在收入或费用所属期间入账，此时现金尚未收付
senses.example: The accountant accrued the rent for December in the year-end books.
senses.exampleCN: 会计在年终账目里把十二月的租金记为应计项目。
senses.why: Accounting borrows the image of growth: the amount has built up during the period, so it is entered even before payment.
senses.whyCN: 会计借用了「生长」的画面：数额在该期间已经长成，所以即便未付款也要入账。

senses.title: Of a legal claim: to become complete
senses.titleCN: （法律请求权）成立；可强制执行
senses.definition: of a right of action, to become complete and enforceable once all the facts that support it have occurred
senses.definitionCN: 指诉权在全部支持事实发生后变得完整并可强制执行
senses.example: The claim for damages accrued when the contract was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 合同被违反时，损害赔偿请求权即告成立。
senses.why: A right is imagined as growing until it is full-grown, and only a full-grown right can be enforced in court.
senses.whyCN: 权利被想象成一个生长过程，长成之后才足够完整，能在法庭上强制执行。

intro.en: Accrue came to English through Old French, and its oldest recorded layer is the Latin verb for growing.
intro.cn: accrue 经古法语进入英语，它最古老的可考层次是表示「生长」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: The Latin verb crescere meant to grow, come into being, and increase; it also lies behind crescent and increase.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 crescere 意为「生长、形成、增加」，crescent 与 increase 也出自它。

items.en: Ad- plus crescere formed accrescere, to grow onto or be added to something. The prefix marks growth toward a thing.
items.cn: ad- 与 crescere 构成 accrescere，意为「长到某物之上、附加于某物」；前缀标记生长所朝向的对象。

items.en: Old French used acreue, the feminine past participle of acreistre, as a noun for growth, increase, or what has grown onto something.
items.cn: 古法语把动词 acreistre 的阴性过去分词 acreue 用作名词，表示「生长、增加、长出来的部分」。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the late fifteenth century, first as a noun and soon after as a verb. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪后期借入这个词，先作名词，随后作动词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The financial sense of interest growing on a sum fixed the word in everyday use, and law and accounting later borrowed the same image.
items.cn: 利息在款项上生长的金融义让这个词进入日常使用，法律与会计随后借用了同一个画面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin root for growing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of piling up and of rights arising.
note.cn: 形近组收以拉丁语「生长」词根构成的一族词；近义组收表示堆积增多与权利产生的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of accumulating, or the amount that has accumulated, especially in accounting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「累积过程、应计额」，多见于会计语境，由本词加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective for money or benefits that have built up but not yet been paid or received.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「应计的、已累积的」，指已积累但尚未收付的钱款或权益。

entries.definition: Growth by gradual addition from outside, as of sediment, ice, or capital; it shares the Latin root crescere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堆积、增积」，指外部物质或资本逐渐附着而增多，与本词同出拉丁语 crescere。

entries.definition: To grow together or be added gradually, used especially of land formed by deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐增长、附着形成」，多用于沉积形成的土地，与本词同根。

entries.definition: To become larger in size, number, or amount; the plain everyday verb of the same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「增加、增大」，是同一拉丁词族中最日常的说法，不带金融色彩。

entries.definition: To gather or pile up more and more of something; it stresses deliberate collecting rather than natural growth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积累、堆积」，强调有意地收集，而非自然生长。

entries.definition: To collect a large amount of something, especially wealth or evidence, over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积聚、搜集」，多指长期攒下大量财富或证据。

entries.definition: To increase steadily in amount or intensity, as of costs, pressure, or opposition.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上升、增加」，多用于成本、压力或反对声浪的持续升高。

entries.definition: To come into being, as of a right, duty, or problem; close to accrue in its legal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「产生、出现」，可用于权利、义务或问题，在法律语境中与 accrue 相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root for growing and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「生长」词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Crescere is to grow: accrue is what happens when an amount quietly grows on a balance.
normal.cn: crescere 是「生长」：accrue 就是数额在账面上悄悄长大的过程。

normal.en: The prefix ac- is a form of ad-, meaning toward, so the growth is directed onto something.
normal.cn: 前缀 ac- 是 ad- 的变体，意为「朝向」，所以这种生长是长到某物之上的。

normal.en: Accrued interest is the standard banking phrase for interest that has built up but not yet been paid.
normal.cn: accrued interest 是银行业的标准说法，指已经积累但尚未支付的利息。

normal.en: Accrue to is the pattern used when a right or benefit falls to a person.
normal.cn: accrue to 是权利或利益落到某人身上时使用的固定结构。

normal.en: The same root gives increase and crescent, both about getting bigger.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 increase 与 crescent，两者都与变大有关。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger page where one line rises a hair each night, like water in a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一页账簿，其中一行每晚悄悄升高一点，像杯中的水。

abstract.en: Nothing is added by hand: the number grows because time passes, and that is the whole idea.
abstract.cn: 没有人手动加数：数字变大只因时间流逝，这就是全部要点。

abstract.en: The same quiet rise can be a debt, a right, or a pile of leave days, not only money.
abstract.cn: 同样安静的上升可以是债务、权利或一堆假期，并不限于金钱。

examples.en: Interest accrues daily on any unpaid balance.
examples.cn: 任何未付余额都按日计息。

examples.en: Benefits accrue to the whole village once the well is finished.
examples.cn: 水井建成后，整个村子都会受益。

examples.en: She let her holiday pay accrue until the end of the year.
examples.cn: 她把假期工资攒到年底再一并领取。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿库鲁」——阿库的账户，利息一点点长高：累积、生息

root: 拉丁语 accrescere「长到、附加」由 ad-「朝向」+ crescere「生长」构成；古法语 acreue 是其过去分词形式的名词化，意为「增长、长出的部分」。crescere 一般认为与 crescent、increase 同源，更早的印欧语形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accrue all picture something growing onto a base: interest, leave, rights, debts, a fund, general quantities, accounting entries, and legal claims.
sensesIntro.cn: accrue 的八个义项都在描绘某物长到某个基底之上：利息、假期、权利、债务、基金、一般数量、会计项目与法律请求权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure on a ledger climbs a little each day, with no hand adding to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上的数字每天自己往上爬一点，没有手在加数。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: interest or fund income grows on a balance that is left alone.
branches.cn: 账目线：利息或基金收益在被搁置的余额上自行生长。

branches.en: THE STORE: anything left to add up, from leave days to advantages, follows the same quiet rise.
branches.cn: 积蓄线：凡是任其累加的东西，从假期到优势，都遵循同一种安静的上升。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: a benefit or claim grows on its holder's side until it is complete and enforceable.
branches.cn: 权利线：利益或请求权在持有者一侧生长，直到完整并可强制执行。

branches.en: THE DEBT: an unpaid charge grows onto a person day by day.
branches.cn: 债务线：未付的费用逐日长到一个人身上。

branches.en: THE BOOKS: accounting records the amount in the period when it has built up, before cash moves.
branches.cn: 账簿线：会计在数额已经长成的期间入账，此时现金尚未流动。

intro.en: Accrue is a French borrowing whose core is the Latin verb for growing; English adds ordinary suffixes to make its family.
intro.cn: accrue 是法语借词，其核心是表示「生长」的拉丁语动词；英语再用普通后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, accrescere and accretio are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere、accrescere 与 accretio 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「生长」指向所生长的对象。

items.example: The verb is the growing root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的「生长」词根。

items.example: Its past participle gave the French noun for growth.
items.exampleCN: 它的过去分词给出了表示「增长」的法语名词。

items.example: It forms increase on the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它与同一词根构成 increase。

definition_en: an amount that is too much, or more than is needed
core_image: 行李秤上超重的箱子
scene: 行李超过了规定重量，她只好为超出的部分付费。 Her bag was over the limit, so she paid for the excess.
sceneCN: 这里 excess 是「超出部分」（第 2 个义项：超过限度的量）；句意：行李超过了规定重量，她只好为超出的部分付费。

senses.title: Too much of something
senses.definition: an amount that is more than is good or needed
senses.definitionCN: 超过适宜或所需的数量
senses.example: An excess of sugar is bad for teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 糖分过量对牙齿有害。
senses.why: The word names what spills past the right amount.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指溢出适宜量的部分。

senses.title: The amount over a limit
senses.definition: the amount by which something is over a limit
senses.definitionCN: 某物超过限度的数量
senses.example: You must pay for any excess.
senses.exampleCN: 超出的部分必须付费。
senses.why: A limit is crossed and the extra stays visible.
senses.whyCN: 越过限度后，多出的部分清晰可见。

senses.title: Extra in a bad way
senses.definition: more than is proper or allowed
senses.definitionCN: 超过适当或被允许的范围
senses.example: The airline charges for excess baggage.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司对超重行李收费。
senses.why: The adjective marks luggage beyond the line.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记超出界限的行李。

intro.en: Excess comes from Latin excessus, a going beyond, from excedere.
intro.cn: excess 源自拉丁语 excessus（越出），来自 excedere。

items.en: Excedere means to go beyond.
items.cn: excedere 意为越过。

items.en: Excessus is a going too far.
items.cn: excessus 意为走得过头。

items.en: French exces keeps the sense of overdoing.
items.cn: 法语 exces 保留过度之意。

items.en: English excess means too much or the extra part.
items.cn: 英语 excess 意为过多或超出部分。

items.en: In excess of becomes a formal phrase.
items.cn: in excess of 成为正式短语。

note.en: Excess is too much; surplus is simply what is left over.
note.cn: excess 指过多，surplus 指单纯剩余下来的部分。

entries.definition: an amount left after needs are met

normalIntro.en: Excess is what crosses the line and stays there.
normalIntro.cn: excess 就是越过界线后多出来的那部分。

normal.en: In excess of means more than.
normal.cn: in excess of 意为超过。

normal.en: Excess baggage costs extra at the airport.
normal.cn: excess baggage 在机场要额外付费。

normal.en: Eat to excess means eat far too much.
normal.cn: eat to excess 意为吃得过多。

normal.en: Excess weight is hard on the body.
normal.cn: excess weight 对身体负担很重。

normal.en: Excessive is the adjective from excess.
normal.cn: excessive 是 excess 的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a cup spilling over its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子从边缘溢出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a suitcase bulging past the scale.
abstract.cn: 想象行李箱鼓出秤面。

abstract.en: Think of a bill with one line too many.
abstract.cn: 想象账单上多出一行。

examples.en: There is an excess of oil in the pan.
examples.cn: 锅里油太多了。

examples.en: The fee is in excess of a hundred dollars.
examples.cn: 费用超过一百美元。

examples.en: He drank to excess at the party.
examples.cn: 他在聚会上喝得过量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ cess（走）」——走出限度的那一部分，就是过量。

root: 拉丁语 excedere（越过）→ excessus（越出）→ excess，核心义「越过界线后多出来的部分」。

sensesIntro.en: Excess is too much of something, the amount over a limit, or an adjective for extra baggage.
sensesIntro.cn: excess 指某物过多、超过限度的部分，或作形容词表示超额的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup spilling over its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：从杯沿溢出的水。

branches.en: Too much is the general sense.
branches.cn: 过多是整体义项。

branches.en: The extra over a limit is measurable.
branches.cn: 超过限度的部分是可计量的。

branches.en: The adjective labels what is over.
branches.cn: 形容词标记超出的东西。

branches.en: What is too much is exactly the extra.
branches.cn: 过多的东西正是多出来的部分。

branches.en: The extra amount becomes excess baggage.
branches.cn: 超出的量变成超重行李。

intro.en: Excess comes from Latin excedere, to go beyond.
intro.cn: excess 来自拉丁语 excedere（越过）。

latinIntro.en: Excessus, a going too far, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: excessus（走得过头）是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: excess 保留了多出的含义。

items.example: The phrase states a limit passed.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语表示越过的限度。

latinEntries.example: Excessus is the source of excess.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excessus 是 excess 的来源。

definition_zh: 嫉妒的；羡慕的；吃醋的；小心守护的
definition_en: unhappy because someone has something you want, or afraid of losing someone's love or attention
core_image: 有人朝你喜欢的人伸出手，你不由地把杯子握得更紧
scene: 聚会上有人和她聊了很久，他在角落里一直盯着那只杯子。 He felt jealous when she laughed with his old friend.
sceneCN: 这里 jealous 是「嫉妒的」（第 1 个义项：因别人得到自己想要的东西而不快），句意为她和他的老朋友说笑时他感到嫉妒。画面里的物件：聚会的杯子、角落、旁人的笑声。

pos.zh: 形容词：嫉妒的；吃醋的；小心守护的

derivatives.zh: 由 jealous 加 -y 构成，义为「嫉妒；吃醋」
由 jealous 加 -ly 构成，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」
由 jealous 加 -ness 构成，义为「嫉妒的状态」

senses.title: Wanting what another has
senses.definition: unhappy and resentful because someone else has something you want
senses.definitionCN: 因别人拥有你想要的东西而不快、怨恨
senses.example: He was jealous of her new car.
senses.exampleCN: 他嫉妒她的新车。
senses.why: This sense grows from the older fear of rivals and is now the commonest use.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项从更古老的「害怕情敌」延伸出来，如今最常用。

senses.title: Afraid of losing love
senses.definition: afraid that someone you love might be more interested in another person
senses.definitionCN: 害怕所爱的人对别人更有兴趣
senses.example: She gets jealous if he talks for long to anyone else.
senses.exampleCN: 只要他跟别人聊久了，她就会吃醋。
senses.why: The rival's jealousy is the oldest thread, kept in the emotional sense we still use.
senses.whyCN: 提防情敌的嫉妒是最古老的一条线，保存在我们今天仍在用的情感义里。

senses.title: Guarding possessively
senses.definition: very careful to protect something you think of as yours
senses.definitionCN: 非常谨慎地守护自己认为是自己的东西
senses.example: The manager is jealous of his team's time.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理很爱惜团队的时间。
senses.why: Guarding closely is the same grip on what one considers one's own, with anger removed.
senses.whyCN: 紧守不放是对「自己之物」的同一种握紧，只是抽掉了愤怒。

senses.title: Envying with respect
senses.definition: admiring another person's good fortune in a way that is slightly painful
senses.definitionCN: 带着一点痛感地羡慕别人的好运
senses.example: I am jealous of your long holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 我羡慕你那么长的假期。
senses.why: In everyday speech the word now covers mild envy as well as resentment.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语里，这个词既指怨恨，也涵盖轻微的羡慕。

senses.title: Protective of an idea
senses.definition: unwilling to let a right or principle be weakened
senses.definitionCN: 不肯让自己的权利或原则被削弱
senses.example: They were jealous of their independence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们非常珍视自己的独立。
senses.why: A community guarding its rights watches them as closely as a jealous keeper guards a door.
senses.whyCN: 守护权利的群体，就像小心看守门的守卫一样看得极紧。

intro.en: Jealous came through Old French gelos from Greek zelos, then Latin zelus, meaning eager rivalry or zeal.
intro.cn: jealous 经古法语 gelos 来自希腊语 zelos、拉丁语 zelus，原义为热烈争胜或热忱。

items.en: zelos meant eager rivalry, zeal, or jealousy.
items.cn: zelos 意为热烈的争胜、热忱或嫉妒。

items.en: zelus kept the same range of eager feeling.
items.cn: zelus 保留了同样一串热切的情感义。

items.en: gelos narrowed the word toward jealousy and love.
items.cn: gelos 把词义收窄到嫉妒与爱情上。

items.en: English took jelus or gelous as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语借入 jelus、gelous 作形容词。

items.en: The same Greek root also gave zeal and zealous.
items.cn: 同一个希腊词根还生出 zeal 与 zealous。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jealous family and the zealous cousin; the near-meaning group holds envy and suspicion.
note.cn: 形近组是 jealous 词族与 zealous 这一同源近亲；近义组收羡慕与猜疑相关词。

entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -y 构成的名词，义为「嫉妒」。

entries.definition: In a jealous or watchful way.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「嫉妒地；小心地」。

entries.definition: Full of energy for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 同源形容词，义为「热心的」，词根同为希腊 zelos。
形容词义为「羡慕的、嫉妒的」，更侧重羡慕。
形容词义为「多疑的」，强调不信任。
形容词义为「占有欲强的」，常用于关系。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie jealous to the Greek root that also produced zeal and zealous.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 jealous 系到同样生出 zeal、zealous 的希腊词根上。

normal.en: Greek zelos meant eager rivalry.
normal.cn: 希腊语 zelos 意为热烈争胜。

normal.en: Zeal and zealous share the same root.
normal.cn: zeal 与 zealous 共用同一词根。

normal.en: Jealous of is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: jealous of 是常见的搭配。

normal.en: Old French gelos pointed the word at love.
normal.cn: 古法语 gelos 把词义指向爱情。

normal.en: To guard jealously is to watch very closely.
normal.cn: guard jealously 就是看得极紧。

abstract.en: Jealousy counts what someone else is holding.
abstract.cn: 嫉妒在数别人手里有的东西。

abstract.en: The tight hand on a cup is the whole feeling.
abstract.cn: 把杯子握紧的那只手就是全部感受。

abstract.en: Watching a door and watching a person look alike.
abstract.cn: 看住门和看住一个人，动作是一样的。

examples.en: She was jealous of her sister's success.
examples.cn: 她嫉妒姐姐的成功。

examples.en: Try not to get jealous when he talks to others.
examples.cn: 他跟别人说话时尽量别吃醋。

examples.en: The country is jealous of its independence.
examples.cn: 这个国家珍视自己的独立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「急了吗」—— 看见别人有，急得直咬牙

root: 希腊语 zelos「热烈争胜；热忱」→ 拉丁语 zelus → 古法语 gelos「嫉妒」→ 中古英语 jelus → 现代英语 jealous。同族有 jealousy、jealously，同源近亲 zeal、zealous。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: wanting another's goods, fearing a rival in love, guarding one's own, mild envy, and valuing a right.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：想要别人之物、怕爱人被抢、守护自己的东西、轻微羡慕，以及珍视某种权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tightening on a cup while someone reaches toward a friend.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人朝你的朋友伸手，你把杯子握得更紧。

branches.en: THE CAR: a new car shining in a neighbour's drive.
branches.cn: 新车这条线：邻居车道上发亮的新车。

branches.en: THE PARTY: a long talk with an old friend.
branches.cn: 聚会这条线：跟老朋友的长时间闲聊。

branches.en: THE TEAM: a manager protecting working hours.
branches.cn: 团队这条线：经理护着工作时间。

branches.en: THE HOLIDAY: a long break that is envied.
branches.cn: 假期这条线：让人羡慕的长假。

branches.en: THE COUNTRY: independence watched day and night.
branches.cn: 国家这条线：日日夜夜守着的独立。

definition_en: a person whose job is to guard prisoners in a jail and control the keys
core_image: 一串钥匙挂在腰带上，每走一步都叮当作响
scene: 夜里看守所的走廊上响起钥匙声，谁都知道有人要开门了。 The jailer unlocked the cell and counted the prisoners.
sceneCN: 这里 jailer 是「狱卒」（第 1 个义项：在监狱里看守犯人的人），句意为狱卒打开牢门清点人数。画面里的物件：钥匙串、走廊、牢门。

pos.zh: 名词：狱卒；看守；监狱管理员

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础名词，义为「监狱」
由 jail 加 -ing 构成，义为「监禁」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「被监禁的」

senses.title: A guard in a jail
senses.definition: a person employed to keep prisoners in a jail and to watch them
senses.definitionCN: 受雇在监狱里看守、监视犯人的人
senses.example: The jailer checked the cells every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 狱卒每小时巡查一次牢房。
senses.why: The -er ending adds a person to jail, so the jailer is the one who runs the jail.
senses.whyCN: -er 词尾在 jail 上加了一个人，于是 jailer 就是管这座监狱的人。

senses.title: A keeper of keys
senses.definition: the person who holds the keys and decides who may go in or out
senses.definitionCN: 掌管钥匙、决定谁能进出的人
senses.example: Only the jailer could open the heavy gate.
senses.exampleCN: 只有狱卒能打开那道厚门。
senses.why: In practice the jailer's power sits on a ring of keys, so the role is defined by them.
senses.whyCN: 实际上狱卒的权力系在一串钥匙上，于是这个身份就由钥匙来定义。

senses.title: An escort of a prisoner
senses.definition: a person who escorts and watches a prisoner outside the jail
senses.definitionCN: 在监狱外押送、看管犯人的人
senses.example: A jailer sat beside the prisoner on the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 一名看守在车上坐在囚犯旁边。
senses.why: The duty follows the prisoner out of the building, so the guard travels with the job.
senses.whyCN: 职责跟着犯人出了大楼，看守于是随行。

senses.title: A figurative keeper
senses.definition: anyone who controls the freedom of another person
senses.definitionCN: 任何控制他人自由的人
senses.example: Fear was the jailer that kept him at home.
senses.exampleCN: 恐惧是把他困在家里的看守。
senses.why: The metaphor strips the uniform and leaves only the act of keeping someone in.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻去掉了制服，只留下「把某人关住」这个动作。

senses.title: A guard in a myth or story
senses.definition: the stock character who watches over a locked place in stories
senses.definitionCN: 故事里看守封闭之处的固定角色
senses.example: In the tale, the old jailer falls asleep at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里那个老狱卒在门口睡着了。
senses.why: Stories keep the older, simpler picture of one man and a set of doors.
senses.whyCN: 故事保留了更古老也更简单的画面：一个人和一串门。

intro.en: Jailer is the English agent noun of jail, built with -er, so its history follows Latin cavea, "cage", into French.
intro.cn: jailer 是 jail 加 -er 构成的英语施事名词，它的历史顺着拉丁语 cavea「笼子」经法语而来。

items.en: cavea meant a cage or a hollow enclosure.
items.cn: cavea 意为笼子或有空腔的围合处。

items.en: jaiole named a prison, with the variant gaiole.
items.cn: jaiole 指监狱，另有变体 gaiole。

items.en: jail, also spelled gayhol, arrived as the name of the building.
items.cn: jail 也写作 gayhol，作为建筑的名称进入英语。

items.en: -er was added to name the keeper of the jail.
items.cn: 中古英语加上 -er 来指管这座监狱的人。

items.en: Jailer and gaoler both survive, with gaoler now rare.
items.cn: jailer 与 gaoler 都还存在，gaoler 已很少用。

note.en: The look-alike group is the jail- family and its gaol- variant; the near-meaning group holds words for guards and keepers.
note.cn: 形近组是 jail- 词族及 gaol- 变体；近义组收表示看守、守卫的词。

entries.definition: The old British spelling of jailer.
entries.definitionCN: 英国旧式拼法，与本词同音同义。
名词义为「监狱」，本词的基础名词。

entries.definition: An informal word for a prisoner who is often in jail.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「常坐牢的人」，同族名词。

entries.definition: A guard in a prison, used especially in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「看守」，英式英语常指监狱看守。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to protect a place or watch people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「卫兵、看守」，最宽泛，来源不同。

entries.definition: The official in charge of a prison.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「典狱长」，是管整座监狱的官。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the -er person ending with the keys and the doors of the building.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 -er 的人物词尾跟这座建筑的钥匙与门连在一起。

normal.en: Jail plus -er is the person who keeps the jail.
normal.cn: jail 加 -er 就是管监狱的人。

normal.en: The gaoler is the old British form of the same word.
normal.cn: gaoler 是同一个词的英国旧拼法。

normal.en: A jailer's keys open every cell.
normal.cn: 狱卒的钥匙能开每一间牢房。

normal.en: A warder is the British cousin of a jailer.
normal.cn: warder 是 jailer 在英式英语里的近亲。

normal.en: The chief jailer runs the whole building.
normal.cn: chief jailer 管着整栋楼。

abstract.en: A jailer is a person turned into a locked door.
abstract.cn: 狱卒就是一个变成锁门的人。

abstract.en: Whoever holds the keys decides who walks out.
abstract.cn: 谁拿钥匙，谁就决定谁能走出去。

abstract.en: Fear can be a jailer with no uniform.
abstract.cn: 恐惧可以是没穿制服的狱卒。

examples.en: The jailer brought bread and water at noon.
examples.cn: 狱卒中午送来了面包和水。

examples.en: A jailer must count the prisoners twice a day.
examples.cn: 狱卒每天要清点两次犯人。

examples.en: The gaoler opened the gate and stood aside.
examples.cn: 那位狱卒打开门，退到了一边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「街了」—— 钥匙一响，街上的人就知道里面有人看门

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a guard in a jail, a keeper of keys, a guard escorting prisoners, a figurative keeper, and the guard of stories.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：狱中看守、钥匙保管人、押送看守、比喻中的看守，以及故事里的狱卒角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of keys swinging from a belt with every step.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串钥匙挂在腰带上，每走一步就响。

branches.en: THE CORRIDOR: an hourly round of the cells.
branches.cn: 走廊这条线：每小时一次牢房巡查。

branches.en: THE GATE: one man who can open it.
branches.cn: 大门这条线：只有他能打开的那道门。

branches.cn: bus 这条线：坐在囚犯旁边的看守。

branches.cn: 恐惧这条线：把一个人关在屋里的东西。

branches.cn: 故事这条线：在门口睡着的老狱卒。

intro.cn: jailer 是词基加施事词尾：法语借来的「监狱」加上英语的 -er。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor cavea "cage" supplies no -er form; the agent ending is purely English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语祖词 cavea「笼子」没有 -er 形式，施事词尾完全是英语的。

definition_en: by mistake, or by chance rather than by plan
core_image: 手指一滑，刚整理好的文件从屏幕上消失
scene: 她一边回消息一边操作，手指一滑，把刚整理好的表格删掉了。 She accidentally deleted the file she had just finished.
sceneCN: 这里的 accidentally 指「无意中」（第 1 个义项：因失误做了本不打算做的事）；句意是她不小心删掉了刚做完的文件。

senses.title: By mistake
senses.definition: does something by mistake that was never intended
senses.definitionCN: 因一时失误做了本来不打算做的事
senses.example: She accidentally deleted the file she had just finished.
senses.exampleCN: 她不小心删掉了刚做完的文件。
senses.why: The ending -ly turns accidental into a word about how an act is done, and the first use is the small slip that damages something.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把 accidental 变成描述「动作怎么做」的副词，最先用于那种手一滑就弄坏东西的失误。

senses.title: By chance
senses.definition: happens through luck or circumstance with no arrangement made
senses.definitionCN: 出于机缘巧合而发生，没有任何预先安排
senses.example: They accidentally met again in a Paris bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在巴黎的一家书店里偶然重逢。
senses.why: Not every unplanned act is a mistake; two people can meet without either doing wrong, so the same adverb also marks pure coincidence.
senses.whyCN: 并非每一件没计划的事都是失误，两个人相遇谁也没做错，于是同一个副词也用来标记纯粹的巧合。

intro.en: The adverb is the adjective accidental with an ending that says how something is done.
intro.cn: 这个副词是形容词 accidental 加上表示「以何种方式」的词尾。

items.en: cadere meant to fall.
items.cn: cadere 意为落下。

items.en: accidere meant to fall upon or happen.
items.cn: accidere 意为降临、发生。

items.en: accidentalis described what was not essential.
items.cn: accidentalis 描述非本质的部分。

items.en: accidental entered English as a word for unplanned qualities.
items.cn: accidental 进入英语，指非计划、非本质的性质。

items.en: -ly formed the adverb used for slips and coincidences alike.
items.cn: 加 -ly 之后形成的副词，同时用于失手与巧合。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accident family; the near-meaning group names unintended and chance action.
note.cn: 形近组是 accident 词族；近义组表示「非故意」与「碰巧」。

entries.definition: without being aware of what one is doing

normalIntro.en: These hints follow the accident family and its root meaning falling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条顺着 accident 词族和它「落下」的词根。

normal.en: accidental is the adjective; -ly tells you how the act was done.
normal.cn: accidental 是形容词，加 -ly 说明动作是怎么做的。

normal.en: the deleted file is the clearest picture of doing something accidentally.
normal.cn: 被删掉的文件，是「无意中做了某事」最清楚的画面。

normal.en: meeting an old friend accidentally carries no blame at all.
normal.cn: 偶然遇见旧友，这里面一点过错都没有。

normal.en: the root cadere, to fall, gives the sense of something dropping in unasked.
normal.cn: 词根 cadere 是落下，带来「不请自来掉下来」的感觉。

normal.en: keep the two uses apart: one is a slip, the other is luck.
normal.cn: 把两种用法分开：一种是失手，一种是运气。

abstract.en: Picture a finger sliding and a file vanishing.
abstract.cn: 想象手指一滑，文件消失。

abstract.en: See two old classmates turn into the same street at once.
abstract.cn: 想象两位老同学同时拐进同一条街。

abstract.en: Think of a coin landing on its edge by pure luck.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币纯凭运气立在了桌面上。

examples.en: She accidentally deleted the file she had just finished.
examples.cn: 她不小心删掉了刚做完的文件。

examples.en: They accidentally met again in a Paris bookshop.
examples.cn: 他们在巴黎的一家书店里偶然重逢。

examples.en: He accidentally knocked the cup off the table.
examples.cn: 他失手把杯子碰下了桌子。

dict_mnemonic.text: accidental（意外的）+ -ly（地）——以「意外」的方式做事，就是 accidentally。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb covers the slip of the hand and the luck of the meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词，既管手上的失手，也管相遇的运气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger slipping and a file disappearing.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指一滑，文件消失。

branches.en: a file deleted with no wish to delete it
branches.cn: 并不想删却删掉的文件

branches.en: a cup knocked over by a passing sleeve
branches.cn: 被衣袖带倒的杯子

branches.en: two people meeting with no appointment
branches.cn: 没有约定却相遇的两个人

branches.en: a discovery made while looking elsewhere
branches.cn: 在别处寻找时的发现

branches.en: both uses share the absence of intent
branches.cn: 两种用法共有的是「没有意图」

intro.en: The word is a Latin root, an adjective ending and an adverb ending stacked together.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁词根、形容词词尾与副词词尾层层叠加而成。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere, to fall, also gives cadence and decay.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cadere（落下）还给出 cadence 与 decay。

definition_en: a date on which something is remembered each year, whether with celebration or with solemn ceremony
core_image: 日历翻回去年折过角的那一页
scene: 两个人坐在小餐馆靠窗的位置，桌上摆着一支点燃的蜡烛。 They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in a small restaurant.
sceneCN: 这里 anniversary 是「周年纪念日」（第 1 个义项：值得庆祝的周年日期）；句意是他们在小餐馆庆祝结婚十周年。

senses.title: A yearly date of celebration
senses.definition: a date each year on which people celebrate something that began then, such as a wedding
senses.definitionCN: 每年到了某件事开始的那一天，人们为之庆祝的日期，如结婚纪念日
senses.example: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in a small restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在小餐馆庆祝结婚十周年。
senses.why: The Latin word joins annus 'year' and vertere 'to turn': the year turns back to the same date, and that return is the anniversary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语来源把 annus「年」与 vertere「转」合在一起：年转回同一天，这次回转就是 anniversary。

senses.title: A yearly date of remembrance
senses.definition: the same date each year used to remember a sad or serious event, often with a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 每年同一日期用于追忆悲伤或重大事件的日子，常伴以仪式
senses.example: The town held a service on the anniversary of the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇在洪水周年那天举行了纪念仪式。
senses.why: The return of the date does not care whether the event was happy, so the same word marks grief as well as joy.
senses.whyCN: 日期的回转并不区分事件的喜悲，因此同一个词既能标记欢乐，也能标记哀悼。

intro.en: Anniversary is a Latin compound meaning 'turning back every year'.
intro.cn: anniversary 是一个拉丁语复合词，意为「每年转回来」。

items.en: annus meant 'year', the base of annual and annuity as well.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，也是 annual 与 annuity 的词基。

items.en: vertere meant 'to turn', and the turning image survives in the word.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，转回的意象一直留在词里。

items.en: anniversarius meant 'returning every year', built from annus and vertere.
items.cn: anniversarius 意为「每年转回的」，由 annus 与 vertere 构成。

items.en: French passed the word into English with its religious sense intact.
items.cn: 法语把这个词传入英语，宗教纪念义随之而来。

items.en: English first used anniversary for a yearly religious observance.
items.cn: 英语最初用 anniversary 指每年的宗教纪念日。

items.en: From the seventeenth century it spread to weddings and then to any yearly date.
items.cn: 十七世纪起它扩展到婚礼，继而泛指任何周年日期。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin word for year; the near-meaning group covers other yearly markers.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「年」的词根；近义组是其他年度标记。

entries.definition: a fixed sum paid each year
the yearly date of one's birth
an act of honouring a person or event
a special anniversary marked with public celebration

normalIntro.en: Take annus 'year', add vertere 'turn', and you get the day the year turns back to.
normalIntro.cn: 取 annus「年」，加上 vertere「转」，得到的就是年转回的那一天。

normal.en: Anniversary joins the Latin words for year and turning.
normal.cn: anniversary 把拉丁语的「年」与「转」合在一起。

normal.en: The plural changes y to i: anniversaries.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 i：anniversaries。

normal.en: A wedding anniversary is the commonest use.
normal.cn: 结婚纪念日是最常见的用法。

normal.en: Say on the anniversary of, not in the anniversary of.
normal.cn: 要说 on the anniversary of，不用 in。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: an-ni-VER-sa-ry.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：an-ni-VER-sa-ry。

abstract.en: See a calendar page folding back to last year.
abstract.cn: 想象日历翻回去年折角的那一页。

abstract.en: See one candle on a small restaurant table.
abstract.cn: 想象小餐馆桌上一支点燃的蜡烛。

abstract.en: See a wreath laid at a memorial.
abstract.cn: 想象纪念碑前放下的花圈。

examples.en: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in a small restaurant.
examples.cn: 他们在小餐馆庆祝结婚十周年。

examples.en: The town held a service on the anniversary of the flood.
examples.cn: 小镇在洪水周年那天举行了纪念仪式。

examples.en: Next month marks the anniversary of the museum's opening.
examples.cn: 下个月是博物馆开馆的周年纪念。

dict_mnemonic.text: ann（年）加 vers（转）加 -ary：一年转回一次的那天，周年纪念日。

root: 来自拉丁语 anniversarius「每年转回的」，由 annus「年」与 vertere「转」构成，经古法语 anniversaire 进入英语；核心义是「一年转回同一天」。

sensesIntro.en: Two uses: a happy yearly date and a solemn one.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种用法：喜庆的周年，与肃穆的周年纪念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar page turning back to the same date.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历翻回同一个日子。

branches.en: a wedding anniversary
branches.cn: 结婚纪念日

branches.en: a tenth anniversary dinner
branches.cn: 十周年纪念晚餐

branches.en: the anniversary of the flood
branches.cn: 洪水周年

branches.cn: 周年当天的纪念仪式

intro.cn: 这是一个由「年」与「转」构成的拉丁语复合词，周围有一小族与年相关的词。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Latin, so the Latin items show how the compound was assembled.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词根都来自拉丁语，因此拉丁词条展示这个复合词是如何拼成的。

definition_zh: 揭开；掀开；发现；揭露；查明
definition_en: to remove a cover, or to find out something that was hidden
core_image: 把盖布一把掀开，底下原本藏着的东西露在光里
scene: 考古队在沙地里刮了一上午，终于露出半块刻着字的石板边缘。 The reporter uncovered a series of secret payments.
sceneCN: 这里 uncover 是「发现、揭露」（第 2 个义项：把藏起来的事查出来）；句意为记者揭露了一连串秘密付款。掀开盖布让底下露出来，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词分词作形容词，义为「无遮盖的；被揭发的」
动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「揭露；发掘」

senses.title: To take a cover off something
senses.definition: to lift or remove the thing lying over an object
senses.definitionCN: 把盖在某物上面的东西提起或拿走
senses.example: He uncovered the pot to let the steam out.
senses.exampleCN: 他把锅盖揭开让蒸汽散出去。
senses.why: The verb is un- plus cover, so it simply undoes the covering.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 un- 加 cover，就是把「盖」这个动作反过来。

senses.title: To find out something hidden
senses.definition: to discover a fact or plan that someone wanted concealed
senses.definitionCN: 发现某人本想隐瞒的事实或计划
senses.example: The audit uncovered serious errors.
senses.exampleCN: 审计查出了严重错误。
senses.why: Once the cover is physically lifted, the figurative cover of secrecy behaves the same way.
senses.whyCN: 盖布既然能被掀开，机密这层盖布也一样。

senses.title: To make a truth public
senses.definition: to bring a hidden wrongdoing into public view
senses.definitionCN: 使隐秘的恶行进入公众视野
senses.example: Two journalists uncovered the whole scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 两名记者揭发了整个计划。
senses.why: Muckrakers and auditors alike use the word once the covering image is in place.
senses.whyCN: 只要「盖布」这个比喻立住了，扒粪记者与审计员都会用这个词。

senses.title: To show a hidden part naturally
senses.definition: of natural forces, to leave something visible by moving what lies over it
senses.definitionCN: 指自然力量把覆盖之物移开，使某物可见
senses.example: The rain uncovered the old stone path.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨把那条古老的石板路冲了出来。
senses.why: Water and wind do the uncovering without any intention at all.
senses.whyCN: 风雨本无意图，却完成了揭开这件事。

senses.title: To leave oneself unprotected
senses.definition: to put a body or a position in the open with no shield
senses.definitionCN: 把身体或阵地放在毫无遮挡之处
senses.example: The soldiers edged forward, uncovered by any wall.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们向前挪动，没有任何墙作掩护。
senses.why: To have no cover is to be uncovered, so the military sense is the literal picture standing alone.
senses.whyCN: 没有掩护就是无遮盖，因此这个军事义只是把字面画面单独摆出来。

intro.en: The word is built in English from un- and cover, whose ultimate source is Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词在英语里由 un- 与 cover 组合而成，而 cover 的源头是拉丁语。

items.en: Cooperire joins com-, fully, and operire, to close or hide, meaning to cover completely.
items.cn: cooperire 由 com-（完全）与 operire（关闭、遮盖）组成，意为完全盖住。

items.en: Old French covrir and a shorter form give English cover.
items.cn: 古法语 covrir 及其较短形式给英语带来 cover。

items.en: Cover appears in English in the twelfth century with the sense of covering a thing.
items.cn: cover 在十二世纪进入英语，意为盖住某物。

items.en: Uncover is formed by plain prefixing, first for physical lifting.
items.cn: uncover 由简单加前缀构成，最初用于实物掀盖。

items.en: From the nineteenth century it is common for exposing scandals.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，用它来指揭发丑闻变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cover stem, and the near-meaning group gathers verbs of disclosure.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cover 词干，近义组汇集表示揭露的动词。

entries.definition: to find for the first time
the extent to which something is covered

normalIntro.en: The word is simply the undo of covering, first of pots and then of secrets.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词不过是「盖」的反动作，先掀锅盖，再掀秘密。

normal.en: Un- plus cover reads as take the cover off, exactly as its letters suggest.
normal.cn: un- 加 cover 读作把盖拿走，正如字面所写。

normal.en: Discover and uncover both build on the same Latin root of hiding.
normal.cn: discover 与 uncover 同建在一个表示「遮盖」的拉丁词根上。

normal.en: Uncovered is also an adjective for a field with nothing over it.
normal.cn: uncovered 也可作形容词，指没有遮盖的空地。

normal.en: Journalists uncover schemes; engineers uncover faults in a design.
normal.cn: 记者揭露阴谋，工程师查设计里的缺陷。

normal.en: The past tense is uncovered, a regular -ed form.
normal.cn: 过去式是 uncovered，规则的加 -ed 形式。

abstract.en: Take a corner of the cloth and lift it in one motion.
abstract.cn: 捏住盖布一角，一下掀起来。

abstract.en: See beneath it something already there, only unknown.
abstract.cn: 看见底下早就在，只是没人知道。

abstract.en: Then watch rain wash soil off an old stone path.
abstract.cn: 再看雨水冲掉石板路上的泥土。

examples.en: The police uncovered a network of false documents.
examples.cn: 警方查出了一个假证件网络。

examples.en: Wind had uncovered the roots of the fallen tree.
examples.cn: 风把倒下的树的根露了出来。

examples.en: She uncovered the tray to show us the cake.
examples.cn: 她把托盘盖掀开，让我们看那块蛋糕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安卡佛」——安好盖子再卡上，一掀开，佛就现身了。

root: un-（反向前缀）+ cover（古法语 covrir，源自拉丁语 cooperire，由 com-「完全」+ operire「遮盖」构成）

sensesIntro.en: All senses undo a covering, whether a lid, a secrecy, a layer of soil, or a shield.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都在解除一层遮盖：锅盖、保密、土层，或掩护。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth pulled back from what lay beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖布被掀开，露出底下的东西。

branches.en: The physical branch: pots, trays, and lids.
branches.cn: 实物分支：锅、托盘与盖子。

branches.en: The inquiry branch: audits and police work that find facts.
branches.cn: 调查分支：审计与侦查查出事实。

branches.en: The public branch: reporters exposing a scheme.
branches.cn: 公开分支：记者揭发阴谋。

branches.en: The nature branch: rain and wind uncovering stone.
branches.cn: 自然分支：风雨冲露出石板。

branches.en: The military branch, where no wall gives cover.
branches.cn: 军事分支：没有墙可作掩护。

intro.en: A reversing prefix on a verb of hiding, itself from Latin.
intro.cn: 反向前缀盖在一个表示遮盖的动词上，该动词源自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Operire, to close, also lies behind cover, covert, and discover.
latinIntro.cn: operire（关闭）还支撑着 cover、covert、discover。

items.exampleCN: uncover 是 cover 的反动作。

items.example: The boat stood uncovered all winter.
items.exampleCN: 那条船整个冬天都露天放着。

items.example: The uncovering of the tomb took years.
items.exampleCN: 这座墓的发掘花了好几年。

definition_zh: 每年的；一年一次的；每年地；一年一次地
definition_en: happening once every year or calculated over a period of one year
core_image: 同一本台历，每年到同一个月份就翻到同一页
scene: 公司财务把一年的账都收进同一个文件夹，每到年底把同一张表再填一遍。 The club holds a yearly meeting in the spring.
sceneCN: 这里 yearly 是「一年一次的」（第 1 个义项：每年发生一次）；句意为俱乐部每年春天开一次会。台历每年翻到同一页，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 year 加 long 构成，义为「持续一年的」
与 yearly 意义相近的拉丁来源副词，义为「每年」

senses.title: Once in each cycle
senses.definition: happening once every year, used of events and arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 每年发生一次，用于事件与安排
senses.example: The club holds a yearly meeting in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部每年春天开一次会。
senses.why: Adding -ly to year turns the cycle into a repeating schedule, so the word says how often.
senses.whyCN: 给 year 加 -ly，就把这个周期变成了重复的日程，于是词说的是多久一次。

senses.title: Counted over one cycle
senses.definition: calculated over a period of one year, used of pay, income, and reports
senses.definitionCN: 按一年的时长来计算，用于薪酬、收入与报告
senses.example: Her yearly income is enough to cover the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她的年收入足够付房租。
senses.why: If a cycle can be repeated, it can also serve as a unit of counting, so totals are added up by year.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个周期可以重复，它也能充作计数的单位，于是总数按年相加。

senses.title: In each cycle
senses.definition: as an adverb, meaning in every year or once a year
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，意为每年或一年一次
senses.example: The magazine is published yearly.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志每年出版一次。
senses.why: The same form serves as an adverb because -ly marks manner and frequency in English, so no change is needed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形式也能作副词，因为 -ly 在英语里既标方式也标频率，不需另加变形。

senses.title: Over the whole of a cycle
senses.definition: covering or lasting for a whole year, said of a period or amount
senses.definitionCN: 持续或涵盖整整一年，用于时段或数量
senses.example: They agreed on a yearly rent for the small shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这家小店谈定了全年租金。
senses.why: A repeating event can also stretch to fill its whole cycle, so the word covers a full year rather than a point in it.
senses.whyCN: 重复发生的事也可以一直铺满整个周期，于是这个词涵盖的是一整年而不是其中的一点。

senses.title: The same as every year
senses.definition: used with verbs to show that something recurs in the same way, as in yearly tradition
senses.definitionCN: 与名词连用时表示情形年年照旧，如 yearly tradition
senses.example: Visiting the old teacher is a yearly tradition for us.
senses.exampleCN: 去看望那位老教师是我们每年的习惯。
senses.why: Since the cycle repeats without change, the word also carries the feeling of a fixed custom.
senses.whyCN: 周期一成不变地重复，于是这个词也带上了固定习俗的意味。

intro.en: Yearly is simply year with the Old English suffix -līc, which became -ly and marked a repeated pattern.
intro.cn: yearly 就是 year 加上古英语后缀 -līc，这个后缀写成 -ly，表示重复的模式。

items.en: gēarlīce was formed from gēar plus the suffix -līce, meaning in the manner of a year.
items.cn: 古英语 gēarlīce 由 gēar 加后缀 -līce 构成，意为「以一年的方式」。

items.en: The suffix reduced to -ly, and year became the first element of a regular adjective.
items.cn: 后缀简化为 -ly，year 成了这个规则形容词的第一个成分。

items.en: The adjective settled alongside the adverb, with the same spelling for both.
items.cn: 形容词与副词并行固定下来，两者拼写相同。

items.en: Yearly was preferred in business and school usage, while annual came in from Latin for formal writing.
items.cn: yearly 多用于商业与学校，正式书面语则用来自拉丁语的 annual。

items.en: Today both forms share the two jobs of describing frequency and counting a full year.
items.cn: 今天这两种形式都兼有表示频率与计算整年的两个用途。

note.en: Yearly is compared with its Latin twin annual and with other frequency words.
note.cn: yearly 常与拉丁来源的 annual 以及表示频率的词对比。

entries.definition: a cycle of about three hundred and sixty-five days

entries.definitionCN: 同根复合词，持续一年的

entries.definition: before the expected time, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，较早，词源不同

entries.definition: happening once a year, from Latin
entries.definitionCN: 近义，拉丁来源的「一年一次的」
同类频率词，每月一次的

normalIntro.en: Yearly shows the everyday English pattern: a time word plus -ly makes a frequency word.
normalIntro.cn: yearly 展示了英语里最常见的构词方式：时间词加 -ly 变成频率词。

normal.en: Swap the base and you get the pattern: month plus -ly is monthly, day plus -ly is daily.
normal.cn: 换掉底词就是同一个模式：month 加 -ly 是 monthly，day 加 -ly 是 daily。

normal.en: The same spelling covers both adjective and adverb, as in yearly report and published yearly.
normal.cn: 同一个拼写兼作形容词和副词，如 yearly report 与 published yearly。

normal.en: Annual does the same job in formal writing, because Latin annus means year.
normal.cn: 正式书面语里 annual 干同样的活，因为拉丁语 annus 就是年。

normal.en: Yearly income is a total gathered over one full cycle, not the money of one moment.
normal.cn: yearly income 是把整个周期加总，而不是某一刻的钱。

normal.en: A yearly tradition borrows the unchanged repetition of the seasons.
normal.cn: yearly tradition 借用了四季一成不变的重复。

abstract.en: Picture a wall calendar whose same page is turned to on the same date every year.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙上的日历，每年同一个日子都翻到同一页。

abstract.en: Picture a folder labelled with one year, filled with exactly one year of bills.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标着年份的文件夹，里面正好装一年的账单。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hand needs a whole year to come back to the same mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个钟，指针要整整一年才回到同一格。

examples.en: The club holds a yearly meeting in the spring.
examples.cn: 俱乐部每年春天开一次会。

examples.en: Her yearly income is enough to cover the rent.
examples.cn: 她的年收入足够付房租。

examples.en: The magazine is published yearly.
examples.cn: 这本杂志每年出版一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一阿里里」——每年结账时票据堆得一「阿里里」，这一年到头的把账算清的活儿，就是 yearly 的每年一次。

root: year（年，古英语 gēar）加后缀 -ly（古英语 -līce，表示以某方式），构成表示频率的形容词与副词。

sensesIntro.en: Turn the cycle into a schedule and the word tells how often, how much, and how long at once.
sensesIntro.cn: 把这个周期变成日程，这个词同时说明了多久一次、多少、以及持续多长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same page of the calendar each year
core.cn: 核心意象：每年翻到日历的同一页

branches.en: A repeated event is the clearest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 重复发生的事件是这个词最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Counting by the cycle turns the word into a unit of total.
branches.cn: 按周期计数，使这个词成为总量的单位。

branches.en: The adverb use states frequency without changing shape.
branches.cn: 副词用法直接说明频率，形式不变。

branches.en: A repeating event can fill its whole cycle, so a full year is covered.
branches.cn: 重复的事可以铺满整个周期，于是涵盖整整一年。

branches.en: Unchanging repetition carries the feeling of custom.
branches.cn: 不变的重复带来习俗的意味。

intro.en: Yearly is built with the productive suffix -ly, which turns time nouns into frequency words.
intro.cn: yearly 由能产后缀 -ly 构成，这个后缀把时间名词变成频率词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for year, annus, gives formal partners such as annual and annually.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「年」的 annus 提供了 annual、annually 等正式对等词。

items.meaningCN: 约三百六十五天的一个周期

items.meaning: forming words such as monthly and daily

definition_en: excellent in quality
core_image: 舞台灯光下完美落幕的一刻
scene: 演出的质量非常出色。 The quality of the performance was superb.
sceneCN: 这里 superb 是「卓越的、极好的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演出的质量非常出色。

senses.title: Excellent in quality
senses.definition: of the very best quality
senses.definitionCN: 质量达到极高水平
senses.example: The quality of the performance was superb.
senses.exampleCN: 演出的质量非常出色。
senses.why: This is the main quality sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的质量义项。

senses.title: Magnificent to see
senses.definition: grand and beautiful to look at
senses.definitionCN: 宏大而美丽，令人赞叹
senses.example: The hall has a superb ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅有壮丽的天花板。
senses.why: Here the word praises appearance.
senses.whyCN: 这里赞的是外观。

intro.en: Superb comes from Latin superbus, proud and magnificent.
intro.cn: superb 来自拉丁语 superbus，意为骄傲而壮丽的。

items.en: Superbus meant proud or magnificent.
items.cn: superbus 意为骄傲的、壮丽的。

items.en: Superbe meant splendid.
items.cn: superbe 意为壮丽的。

items.en: Superb meant splendid in appearance.
items.cn: superb 意为外观壮丽的。

items.en: It came to mean excellent in quality.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示质量卓越。

items.en: It is stronger than good.
items.cn: 它的语气比 good 更强。

note.en: Superb is compared with look-alike words and with words for excellence.
note.cn: 把 superb 与形近词以及表示优秀的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Superb is excellence that makes people stop and look.
normalIntro.cn: superb 是让人停下来观看的卓越。

normal.en: The quality of the performance was superb.
normal.cn: 演出的质量非常出色。

normal.en: The view from the hill was superb.
normal.cn: 从山上看到的景色美极了。

normal.en: She cooked a superb meal.
normal.cn: 她做了一顿极好的饭。

normal.en: The hall has a superb ceiling.
normal.cn: 大厅有壮丽的天花板。

normal.en: His skill with the violin is superb.
normal.cn: 他的小提琴技艺高超。

abstract.en: Superb is good with no apology in it.
abstract.cn: 卓越，是不带一丝歉意的优秀。

abstract.en: Excellence is a habit before it is a result.
abstract.cn: 卓越先是一种习惯，然后才是结果。

abstract.en: The best work often looks effortless.
abstract.cn: 最好的作品，往往看起来不费力气。

examples.en: The quality of the performance was superb.
examples.cn: 演出的质量非常出色。

examples.en: The view from the hill was superb.
examples.cn: 从山上看到的景色美极了。

examples.en: She cooked a superb meal.
examples.cn: 她做了一顿极好的饭。

dict_mnemonic.text: superb 表示质量卓越、极好的，比 good 语气更强；superb quality 是卓越品质，superb view 是壮丽景色。

root: 来自拉丁语 superbus（骄傲的、壮丽的），经法语 superbe 进入英语，由壮丽引申为质量卓越。

sensesIntro.en: Superb means excellent in quality, or magnificent to see.
sensesIntro.cn: superb 表示质量卓越，或外观壮丽。

core.en: Quality that stands above the rest.
core.cn: 高出其余的质量。

branches.en: The quality of the performance was superb.
branches.cn: 演出的质量非常出色。

branches.en: She cooked a superb meal.
branches.cn: 她做了一顿极好的饭。

branches.en: The hall has a superb ceiling.
branches.cn: 大厅有壮丽的天花板。

branches.en: Skill and beauty can both be superb.
branches.cn: 技艺与美都可以是卓越的。

branches.en: The view from the hill was superb.
branches.cn: 从山上看到的景色美极了。

intro.en: Superb builds superbly and shares the super- family.
intro.cn: superb 可构成 superbly，并与 super- 词族同源。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin superbus, proud.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是拉丁语 superbus，意为骄傲的。

items.example: The superbness of the work was clear.

items.exampleCN: 他们证明了自己的优越。
这个故事有超自然元素。

latinEntries.example: Superbus is the source of superb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: superbus 是 superb 的来源。
super 是 superbus 的词根。

definition_en: a man who works with his hands in a trade, judged by the quality of his work
core_image: 一个钉子被敲三下正好齐平，不用再补
scene: 木器铺的老师傅做完一张凳子，用手掌沿边抹了一圈，确认没有毛刺。 A good workman is known by the joints you cannot see.
sceneCN: 这里 workman 是「工匠、技术工人」（第 1 个义项：用手艺吃饭的人）；句意为好工匠凭的是你看不见的接缝来见本事。敲三下正好齐平的那颗钉子，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: a bad workman blames his tools

derivatives.zh: 由 workman 加 -ship 构成，义为「手艺；做工」
由 workman 加 -like 构成，义为「像工匠干出来的；干练的」
词根动词，义为「工作；干活」

senses.title: The hand that works
senses.definition: a man employed in a trade that calls for his hands and his skill
senses.definitionCN: 在需要手艺与双手的行业里受雇的男人
senses.example: The old workman raised the beam with three men and a rope.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老工匠带着三个人和一根绳子把横梁抬了起来。
senses.why: The compound joins work with man in its old sense of person, so it names a person whose life is the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 work 与旧义为「人」的 man 结合，指以工作为生的人。

senses.title: The standard of the craft
senses.definition: the quality shown by what such a person makes, in phrases like a good workman
senses.definitionCN: 由此人做出来的东西体现的手艺水准，如 a good workman
senses.example: A good workman is known by the joints you cannot see.
senses.exampleCN: 好工匠凭你看不见的接缝来见本事。
senses.why: Here the word stops naming a person and names the standard that the person meets.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不再指人，而指此人所达到的那条手艺标准。

senses.title: The one who blames the tool
senses.definition: used in the saying that a bad workman blames his tools, meaning skill matters more than equipment
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语「a bad workman blames his tools」，意即本事比工具更重要
senses.example: When the shelf came out crooked he blamed the saw, but a bad workman blames his tools.
senses.exampleCN: 架子做得歪了，他便怪那把锯子，可是手笨的人才怨工具。
senses.why: A word for the skilled hand easily becomes part of a saying about the unskilled one.
senses.whyCN: 一个指巧手的词，很容易就成了一句话里指笨手的部分。

intro.en: Workman joins Old English weorc, work, with mann, a person; only much later did man narrow to males.
intro.cn: workman 由古英语 weorc（劳作）与 mann（人）结合；man 很晚才收窄为只指男性。

items.en: weorc and mann could combine freely, and the compound named a person who labours.
items.cn: weorc 与 mann 能自由组合，复合词用来指劳作的人。

items.en: Spelling settled as workman, and the trade sense grew with the guilds.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 workman，随着行会兴起了行业手艺之义。

items.en: The word became the mark of a man judged by the finish of his work.
items.cn: 这个词成了以成品好坏来评断的人的标记。

items.en: The suffix -ship built workmanship for the skill itself.
items.cn: 后缀 -ship 造出 workmanship 来指手艺本身。

items.en: In current use worker is far more common, and workman survives mostly in trade and proverb.
items.cn: 今天 worker 更常用，workman 主要留在行业语与谚语中。

note.en: The first group holds the same stem and its compounds, the second holds other names for a skilled hand.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干及其复合词，第二组收其他指手艺人的称呼。

entries.definition: The skill shown in what is made.
Done in a competent, solid way.
A person skilled in a craft.
A person who repairs and maintains machines.
A skilled worker who makes things by hand in small numbers.

normalIntro.en: Workman is work plus man, and it keeps the old man that meant person, not male.
normalIntro.cn: workman 是 work 加 man，这里的 man 仍是「人」，不是「男人」。

normal.en: The plural is workmen, with a vowel change and no second e.
normal.cn: 复数是 workmen，元音变化且不再多加 e。

normal.en: Workmanship adds -ship for the skill, not for the person.
normal.cn: workmanship 加 -ship 指手艺，不是指人。

normal.en: The proverb about a bad workman blaming his tools is the phrase you will meet most.
normal.cn: 最常见的是那句「手笨怨工具」的谚语。

normal.en: Worker has largely replaced workman in normal writing.
normal.cn: 在一般写作中 worker 已基本取代 workman。

normal.en: Workmanlike means solid rather than brilliant: good, plain, finished.
normal.cn: workmanlike 指扎实而非出色：好、朴素、做完了。

abstract.en: A nail driven in three strokes, exactly flush.
abstract.cn: 三下敲平的一颗钉子。

abstract.en: A palm run along an edge to feel for rough grain.
abstract.cn: 手掌沿边抹过，感觉有没有毛刺。

abstract.en: Joints you cannot see holding the whole frame.
abstract.cn: 看不见的接缝撑住整个框架。

examples.en: The workmen finished the roof before the rain came.
examples.cn: 工匠们在雨来之前把屋顶修完了。

examples.en: The table shows the workmanship of an older generation.
examples.cn: 这张桌子显出上一代人的手艺。

examples.en: A bad workman blames his tools, my grandfather used to say.
examples.cn: 我爷爷常说，手笨的人才怨工具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我克门」——一扇一扇门都靠我克出来的人，就是工匠。

root: 古英语 weorc（劳作）+ mann（人）→ workman；-ship 构成 workmanship（手艺），-like 构成 workmanlike。

sensesIntro.en: The person comes first, then the quality of what he makes, and finally the proverb about the one who blames his tools.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是指人，再是此人做成之物的品质，最后是那句关于怨工具之人的谚语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nail driven in exactly flush.
core.cn: 核心意象：钉子敲得正好齐平。

branches.en: The trade branch: workmen lifting a beam by rope.
branches.cn: 行业分支：用绳抬梁的工匠。

branches.en: The craft branch: joints that hold without showing.
branches.cn: 手艺分支：看不出却撑得住的接缝。

branches.en: The proverb branch: blaming the saw for a crooked shelf.
branches.cn: 谚语分支：架子歪了怪锯子。

branches.en: The reputation branch: a worker known by his finish.
branches.cn: 名声分支：以成品见本事的工人。

branches.en: The judgement branch: skill is praised or blamed by results.
branches.cn: 评断分支：本事靠结果被夸奖或责怪。

intro.en: Workman is a compound of two native words, and the endings -ship and -like build its two adjectives and nouns.
intro.cn: workman 是两个本土词的复合，-ship 与 -like 造出它的名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin; the words below belong to other languages that also name a skilled hand.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都不是拉丁语；下面的词属其他语言，同样指有手艺的人。

items.exampleCN: 它给出 workmen 而非 workmans。

items.example: It builds craftsmanship in some uses.
items.exampleCN: 有些用法中由它构成 craftsmanship。

definition_en: a short test of knowledge; a game in which people answer questions; to ask a person a series of questions
core_image: 一叠翻到背面等着写答案的小纸片
scene: 教室里，老师把一叠小纸片发下来，大家翻到背面开始写答案。 We had a short quiz on irregular verbs before the lesson began.
sceneCN: 这里 quiz 是「小测验」（第 1 个义项：检查知识的简短测试）；句意为正式上课前我们先做了一次不规则动词的小测验。画面里可留意：发下来的纸片、翻面的动作、还没开始的课本。

pos.zh: 小测验；知识问答；智力竞赛

derivatives.zh: quiz 加 -er，指参加问答或喜欢做小测的人
与 quiz 同族，指带着疑问、略带打趣的表情
quizzical 加 -ly，指带着疑问神情地

senses.title: A short test of knowledge
senses.definition: a brief test given to check what someone has learned
senses.definitionCN: 为检查学习情况而进行的简短测试
senses.example: We had a quiz on irregular verbs this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们今天早上做了一次不规则动词的小测。
senses.why: The word entered American English as a term for an odd person or a bit of fun, and the test sense grew from playful questioning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初以美式英语俚语身份出现，指古怪的人或一场玩笑，而「测验」义从这种嬉戏式的发问生长出来。

senses.title: A question-and-answer game
senses.definition: a game or show in which people compete by answering questions
senses.definitionCN: 人们通过回答问题来竞争的游戏或节目
senses.example: She won the pub quiz with her team.
senses.exampleCN: 她和队友一起赢了酒吧问答比赛。
senses.why: A quiz as a form of entertainment keeps the older playful tone: questions are asked for fun, not for a grade.
senses.whyCN: 作为娱乐形式的 quiz 保留了较早的嬉戏语气：提问是为了好玩，而不是为了打分。

senses.title: To ask someone many questions
senses.definition: to put a series of questions to a person, often to test or press them
senses.definitionCN: 向某人连续发问，常常是为了检验或施压
senses.example: The reporter quizzed the minister about the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 记者就新税向部长连续发问。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction of the noun: instead of answering questions, the subject is the one who fires them.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的方向颠倒过来：主语不再是回答问题的学生，而是连续抛出问题的人。

intro.en: Quiz is a word of uncertain origin that appeared in English only in the late eighteenth century, probably as slang; no reliable Latin source can be given.
intro.cn: quiz 来源不确定，直到十八世纪后期才在英语中出现，很可能是俚语；无法给出可靠的拉丁语来源。

items.en: The first records of quiz come from late eighteenth-century English, and dictionaries disagree about which slang use came first.
items.cn: quiz 的最早记录出现在十八世纪后期的英语中，各家词典对哪一种俚语用法在先并不一致。

items.en: The word was first used for an odd or eccentric person, and also for a joke or a piece of mockery.
items.cn: 这个词最初用来指古怪的人，也用来指玩笑或嘲弄。

items.en: In the nineteenth century quiz settled into the sense of a set of questions used to test knowledge.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，quiz 固定为「用来考查知识的一组问题」这一义项。

items.en: Schools made the quiz a short test, while radio and later television made it a popular question game.
items.cn: 学校把 quiz 做成简短测验，电台以及后来的电视又把它做成大众问答游戏。

items.en: Modern English uses quiz for a short test, for a quiz show and for the act of questioning someone closely.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quiz 指小测、问答节目以及紧追不舍地提问这一行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built from the same short word; the near-meaning group gathers words for tests and questioning.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个短词构成的形式；近义组收表示测验与提问的词。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in quizzes.

entries.definitionCN: 带着轻微怀疑或打趣的。

entries.definition: The act of asking a series of questions.
A set of questions used to measure knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 用来衡量知识的一组问题。

entries.definition: A sentence that asks for information.
To question someone thoroughly and formally.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底而正式地审问某人。

normalIntro.en: The word came from slang for a joke or an odd person, and the playful questioning at its heart became the school quiz and the quiz show.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词源自表示玩笑或怪人的俚语，其核心的嬉戏式发问后来变成学校小测与问答节目。

normal.en: Quiz, quizzes, quizzed: the doubled z is kept so the vowel stays short, as in a quiz but two quizzes.
normal.cn: quiz、quizzes、quizzed：双写 z 是为了保持短元音，所以一个 quiz，两个 quizzes。

normal.en: A pop quiz is one you did not prepare for, which is exactly why it is called pop.
normal.cn: a pop quiz 指你没准备的突击测验，正如 pop 一词所暗示的突然。

normal.en: Quiz show and quiz master name the television version of the same question game.
normal.cn: quiz show 与 quiz master 指同一个问答游戏的电视版本。

normal.en: To quiz a person is to ask question after question, as a reporter quizzes a minister.
normal.cn: to quiz 一个人就是接连发问，就像记者追问部长那样。

normal.en: A quiz is usually short and informal, while an exam is long and formal.
normal.cn: quiz 通常短而不正式，而 exam 长而正式。

abstract.en: A quiz measures what can be recalled under pressure, not everything a person knows.
abstract.cn: 测验衡量的是压力下能回想起来的部分，而非一个人所知的全部。

abstract.en: The same word serves a classroom and a television studio because both turn knowledge into a game.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既用于教室也用于演播室，因为两者都把知识变成游戏。

abstract.en: Being quizzed is being asked to justify yourself in someone else's order of questions.
abstract.cn: 被盘问，就是被要求按别人设定的问题顺序为自己作解释。

examples.en: The teacher gave us a ten-minute quiz at the end of class.
examples.cn: 老师在课末给了我们一次十分钟的小测。

examples.en: Our team came second in the science quiz.
examples.cn: 我们队在科学问答比赛中得了第二。

examples.en: Reporters quizzed the coach about the sudden change of players.
examples.cn: 记者们就突然换人的事追问教练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「窥子」——老师从小纸片里窥见你记住了多少，记住 quiz 是小测验。

root: 来源不确定，通常认为出自十八世纪后期英语俚语，先指怪人或玩笑，后转指一问一答的测验；没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is playful questioning; the senses divide into a short school test, a question game and the act of pressing someone with questions.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是嬉戏式的发问；义项分为学校小测、问答游戏，以及连续向某人施压提问的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of small cards turned face down, waiting for answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠翻到背面、等着写答案的小卡片。

branches.en: a card turned over on a desk
branches.cn: 桌上翻过来的一张卡片

branches.en: buzzers on a television stage
branches.cn: 电视舞台上的一排抢答器

branches.en: a reporter holding a recorder forward
branches.cn: 记者把录音笔伸向前方

branches.en: the same questions asked for a grade and for fun
branches.cn: 同样的问题，一次为分数，一次为乐趣

branches.en: questions that entertain an audience and questions that press a witness
branches.cn: 取悦观众的问题与向证人施压的问题

intro.en: The word is too recent to have a Latin structure; what it does have is a short English root and a set of endings and compounds built on it.
intro.cn: 这个词出现得太晚，没有拉丁语结构；它有的是一个简短的英语词根，以及在此基础上构成的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_en: in the past, before now, or previously
core_image: 一本旧相册翻开，照片里的街道已经变了样
scene: 这个镇以前是个渔村。 The town was formerly a fishing village.
sceneCN: 这里 formerly 是「以前」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个镇以前是个渔村。

senses.title: In earlier times
senses.definition: in a period before the present
senses.definitionCN: 在当前时期之前
senses.example: The town was formerly a fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇以前是个渔村。
senses.why: This is the broad time sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是宽泛的时间义项。

senses.title: Previously in a role
senses.definition: in a previous job or position
senses.definitionCN: 在以前的工作或职位上
senses.example: She formerly worked as a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 她原先做过护士。
senses.why: A person carries old roles into the present.
senses.whyCN: 人会把旧角色带进现在。

senses.title: Under an old name
senses.definition: under a name used in the past
senses.definitionCN: 以过去使用过的名称
senses.example: The city was formerly called by another name.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市从前另有名字。
senses.why: Official history loves this word.
senses.whyCN: 官方历史叙述很喜欢用这个词。

intro.en: Formerly is former plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: formerly 就是 former 加上副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Forma meant first.
items.cn: forma 意为第一。

items.en: Former meant earlier.
items.cn: former 意为较早的。

items.en: Formerly appeared as its adverb.
items.cn: formerly 作为它的副词形式出现。

items.en: It became common in official histories.
items.cn: 它在官方历史叙述中变得常见。

items.en: The phrase formerly known as spread widely.
items.cn: formerly known as 这一说法广泛传播。

note.en: Formerly is compared with its look-alike formally and with words for the past.
note.cn: 把 formerly 与形近词 formally 以及表示过去的词作比较。

entries.definition: at some time in the past

normalIntro.en: Formerly is a window that opens only onto the past.
normalIntro.cn: formerly 是一扇只朝过去打开的窗。

normal.en: The town was formerly a fishing village.
normal.cn: 这个镇以前是个渔村。

normal.en: She formerly worked as a nurse.
normal.cn: 她原先做过护士。

core.en: Time viewed from the far side of change.

branches.en: The place had a different life.

definition_en: shared by a whole group, not special or branded
core_image: 货架上并排放着昂贵的名牌药和便宜的通用名药盒
scene: 医生开了一种便宜的通用名药物。 The doctor prescribed a cheap generic drug.
sceneCN: 这里 generic 是「无商标的；通用名的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：医生开了一种便宜的通用名药物。

senses.title: Shared by a group
senses.definition: general rather than specific, applying to a whole group
senses.definitionCN: 笼统而非特定的，适用于整个类别
senses.example: The report uses a generic term for all such cases.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用了一个统称来指所有这类情况。
senses.why: Generic marks what belongs to a whole kind, not one member.
senses.whyCN: generic 标记的是属于整个类别的特征，而不是某一个成员。

senses.title: Without a brand
senses.definition: a product, especially a drug, sold without a brand name
senses.definitionCN: 不使用品牌名销售的产品，尤指药物
senses.example: The doctor prescribed a cheap generic drug.
senses.exampleCN: 医生开了一种便宜的通用名药物。
senses.why: An unbranded product is named only by its kind.
senses.whyCN: 无品牌产品只用它所属的种类来命名。

senses.title: Of a genus
senses.definition: relating to a genus in the classification of living things
senses.definitionCN: 与生物分类中的「属」有关的
senses.example: The generic name comes before the species name.
senses.exampleCN: 属名写在种名之前。
senses.why: In biology the genus is the group that a species belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学中，属是物种所归属的类别。

intro.en: Generic comes from Latin genus, meaning kind or race.
intro.cn: generic 来自拉丁语 genus，意为种类或族类。

items.en: Genus meant kind, family, or race.
items.cn: genus 意为种类、家族或族类。

items.en: Genericus meant belonging to a kind.
items.cn: genericus 意为属于某一类的。

items.en: It entered English meaning characteristic of a class.
items.cn: 它进入英语时意为某一类别的典型特征。

items.en: Trade law gave it the sense of unbranded goods.
items.cn: 商标法赋予了它无品牌商品的含义。

items.en: Biology kept the sense of belonging to a genus.
items.cn: 生物学保留了它「属于某一属」的含义。

note.en: Generic is compared with look-alike words and words for things that are common.
note.cn: 把 generic 与形近词以及表示常见事物的词作比较。

normalIntro.cn: generic 指向的是整个类别，而不是个体。

abstract.en: A generic answer fits everything and settles nothing.
abstract.cn: 笼统的回答什么都能套，却什么也解决不了。

abstract.en: Names without a brand still name a need.
abstract.cn: 没有品牌的名字，仍然指向一种需要。

abstract.en: The kind is a crowd; the species is a face.

dict_mnemonic.text: generic 与 genus（属、种类）同源：属于整个「种类」的，就是「通用的」；不带品牌的药叫 generic drug，生物分类中的属名叫 generic name。

root: 来自拉丁语 genus（种类、族类）的形容词形式 genericus，核心义「属于某一类的」。

sensesIntro.en: Generic means shared by a whole group, sold without a brand, or belonging to a biological genus.
sensesIntro.cn: generic 意为整个类别共有的、无品牌销售的，或属于生物分类中某一属的。

core.en: Belonging to the whole kind rather than one special case.
core.cn: 属于整个类别，而不是某个特殊个案。

branches.en: A label says only what the whole group shares.
branches.cn: 标签只写出整个群体共有的特征。

branches.en: A plain box sits beside a costly brand.
branches.cn: 朴素的盒子摆在昂贵的品牌旁边。

branches.en: Scientists sort living things by shared traits.
branches.cn: 科学家按共有特征给生物分类。

branches.en: The common and the unbranded are close cousins.
branches.cn: 通用的与无品牌的是一对近亲。

branches.en: Shared features define both goods and species.
branches.cn: 共有特征既定义商品，也定义物种。

intro.en: Generic belongs to the Latin family of genus, kind, and classification.
intro.cn: generic 属于拉丁语 genus（种类、分类）这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus, genitive generis, means kind or race.

definition_en: in a way that reverses what has just been said
core_image: 一枚硬币翻到另一面，图案正好相反
scene: 北边下雪时，南方正晒着太阳，老师让学生把两地说法对调。 The north is cold; conversely, the south is warm.
sceneCN: 这里 conversely 指「反过来」（第 1 个义项：引出与上文相反的说法）；句意是北方寒冷，反过来南方温暖。

senses.title: The other way round
senses.definition: used to introduce a statement that reverses the one just made
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出与刚才所说相反的一句话
senses.example: The north is cold; conversely, the south is warm.
senses.exampleCN: 北方寒冷，反过来，南方温暖。
senses.why: A coin has two faces, and naming one calls up the other.
senses.whyCN: 硬币有两面，说出一面就唤起了另一面。

senses.title: In inverse relation
senses.definition: used when two things move in opposite directions
senses.definitionCN: 用于两件事朝相反方向变化的情形
senses.example: Costs fell and, conversely, profits rose.
senses.exampleCN: 成本下降，反之利润上升。
senses.why: A seesaw shows that one end must sink for the other to lift.
senses.whyCN: 跷跷板说明一端必须下沉，另一端才会升起。

intro.en: Conversely is converse plus -ly; converse comes from Latin conversus, turned around, from com-, together, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: conversely 由 converse 加 -ly 构成；converse 来自拉丁语 conversus（转向的），由 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn or change direction.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动或改变方向。

items.en: Conversus described something turned right round.
items.cn: conversus 形容某物被完全转过来。

items.en: English converse meant turned about or opposite.
items.cn: 英语 converse 意为转过来的、相反的。

items.en: The adverb conversely was formed to mark an opposite step in an argument.
items.cn: 副词 conversely 形成，用来在论述中标出一个相反的步骤。

items.en: It now usually opens a sentence that mirrors the one before.
items.cn: 今天它通常引出一个与上一句相对照的句子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vers-, and the meaning group names other ways of stating an opposite.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vers-，近义组列出其他表示相反的说法。

entries.definition: the act of changing into another form
to turn something the opposite way
in the opposite order or relation
in a way that goes against what was said

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a coin turned over, then move to two facts pulling in opposite directions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一枚翻面的硬币开始，再到两件事朝相反方向拉扯。

normal.en: Converse is the opposite side, and -ly makes it an adverb, so conversely means on the opposite side.
normal.cn: converse 是相反的一面，加上 -ly 成为副词，conversely 就是在相反的一面。

normal.en: It always points back at the sentence you just read.
normal.cn: 它总是回头指向你刚读过的那句话。

normal.en: Think of a mirror placed beside a statement.
normal.cn: 想象在一句话旁边立起一面镜子。

normal.en: The signal is simple: the next clause will contradict the last.
normal.cn: 信号很简单：下一个分句会与上一个相反。

normal.en: It is the written cousin of saying on the other hand.
normal.cn: 它是书面语里的另一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a page turned over to show the back.
abstract.cn: 想象把一页纸翻过来露出背面。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows sharing one line and pointing apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两条箭头共用一条线，却指向两边。

abstract.en: Picture a scale tipping the other way.
abstract.cn: 想象天平朝另一边倾斜。

examples.en: The days grew shorter; conversely, the nights grew longer.
examples.cn: 白天变短了，反过来，夜晚变长了。

examples.en: Rich soil holds water well and, conversely, sandy soil drains fast.
examples.cn: 肥沃的土壤保水好，反过来，沙土排水快。

examples.en: Conversely, a quiet room can make a small sound seem loud.
examples.cn: 反过来，安静的房间会让轻微的声音显得很响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conversely 记成 converse（相反的）加 ly：以相反的方式说话，就是反过来。

root: 源自拉丁语 vertere（转）的过去分词 conversus（转过来的），加副词词尾 -ly，表示把话头转到相反的一面。

sensesIntro.en: From a single claim turned over, to two quantities moving in opposite directions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把一句话翻到反面，到两个量朝相反方向变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin flipped to show its other face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币翻过来露出另一面。

branches.en: A statement is reversed and set beside the first.
branches.cn: 一句话被反转，放在第一句旁边。

branches.en: Two quantities move apart, one rising as one falls.
branches.cn: 两个量彼此分开，一个升时一个降。

branches.en: Both uses mark a turn to the opposite side.
branches.cn: 两种用法都标记着转向相反的一面。

branches.en: The adverb keeps the reader from missing the reversal.
branches.cn: 这个副词让读者不会漏掉这次反转。

branches.en: It also signals a fixed inverse link between two facts.
branches.cn: 它也标示两件事之间固定的反向联系。

intro.en: Conversely is converse plus the adverb ending -ly, both resting on Latin vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: conversely 由 converse 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，二者都源于拉丁语 vertere（转）。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vert- also appears in convert, reverse and version.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vert- 也出现在 convert、reverse 与 version 中。

items.exampleCN: 反过来，这条规则可能失效。
