definition_zh: 百万；大量；无数；巨额财富
definition_en: the number one million, and by extension an indefinitely large number or a fortune of that size
core_image: 拍卖台上那块号牌一路往上翻，最后停在一串让人不敢念出声的零
scene: 拍卖行的大厅里安静得能听见翻页声，台上的旧画出价一路攀升，最后停在一个谁都没敢喊出的数。 The final bid passed a million and the room let out a breath.
sceneCN: 这里是「百万」这个数目（第 1 个义项：一百万）；句意为最后一次出价越过了百万，全场才松下一口气。图中可辨识物件：拍卖台、木槌、举起的号牌、翻动的价目屏。

collocations.zh: 百万分之一的机会；几乎不可能

derivatives.zh: million 加 -aire（表人后缀）构成，义为「百万富翁」
million 加序数词尾 -th 构成，义为「第一百万个；百万分之一」
multi-（多）加 million 构成，义为「数百万的」

senses.title: The number one million
senses.definition: the exact number that equals one thousand thousands, written as a one followed by six zeros
senses.definitionCN: 精确等于一千个一千的数，写出来是一个后面跟六个零的数字
senses.example: The stadium holds a million people on a match day.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛日这座体育场能容纳一百万人。
senses.why: Mille in Latin means a thousand, and Italian added the augmentative suffix -one to produce a big thousand; the word was coined to name a sum that early speakers could barely count to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mille 是「千」，意大利语又加上增大后缀 -one，造出一个「大一号的千」；这个词被造出来，正是为了命名一个早期使用者几乎数不到的数目。

senses.title: A very great but uncounted number
senses.definition: an indefinitely large number of people or things, used when the exact count does not matter
senses.definitionCN: 数不清的大量人或物，用于说不上具体数目的时候
senses.example: Millions of birds cross this coast every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天都有数以百万计的鸟飞越这片海岸。
senses.why: Once the word pins down one exact million, it can also be loosened to mean any crowd past counting, because the number itself already sits at the edge of what a person can picture.
senses.whyCN: 当 million 先钉住一个精确的数，它也可以松开来指任何数不清的一大群，因为这个数本身就站在人还能想象的范围边缘。

senses.title: A fortune of that size
senses.definition: a very large amount of money, especially when spoken of as the goal or the price of something
senses.definitionCN: 一笔很大的钱，尤指被当作目标或代价谈起的时候
senses.example: He made his millions in shipping and gave much of it away.
senses.exampleCN: 他在航运业赚得巨额财富，又把其中许多捐了出去。
senses.why: A million pounds or dollars is the smallest sum that sounds like freedom, so the noun slid from the number to the fortune it stands for, and the plural carries that sense most easily.
senses.whyCN: 一百万镑或一百万美元，是最像一个「自由」门槛的数目，于是这个名词从数字滑向它所代表的财产，复数形式最容易带上这层意思。

intro.en: Million is a Romance coinage: a Latin thousand took an Italian suffix that made it mean a big thousand, then passed through French into English.
intro.cn: million 是罗曼语系的造词：拉丁语的「千」加上一个意大利语后缀，变成「大一号的千」，再经法语进入英语。

items.en: Mille was the Latin word for a thousand and the source of the whole family of million words.
items.cn: mille 是拉丁语里的「千」，也是整族 million 词的源头。

items.en: The neuter plural millia meant thousands and supplied the pattern for naming a very large counted mass.
items.cn: 中性复数 millia 意为「数以千计」，为命名极大的计数群体提供了样式。

items.en: Italian speakers are generally credited with coining milioni in the thirteenth century by adding the augmentative suffix -one to mille, so that a million was literally a big thousand.
items.cn: 一般认为，意大利语在十三世纪把增大后缀 -one 加到 mille 上造出 milioni，「百万」字面上就是一个「大一号的千」。

items.en: French took the Italian word as million and used it in accounts and records before passing it on to English.
items.cn: 法语把意大利语词取作 million，先在账目与记录里使用，再传给英语。

items.en: English million first named the exact number, then stretched into millions of and a million to one, all built on the idea of a crowd too big to count.
items.cn: 英语的 million 先指精确的数，后来伸展出「数以百万计」「百万分之一」等说法，都建立在「大到数不清」这个念头上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the words built on the same Latin thousand and the same Italian suffix; the near-meaning group gathers the number words above and below it on the same scale.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个拉丁语「千」和同一个意大利语后缀构成的词；近义组收同一把数轴上比它高和比它低的数词。

entries.definition: A person whose wealth reaches a million or more in the local currency.
entries.definitionCN: 财富达到一百万或更多当地货币单位的人。

entries.definition: The ordinal that marks the position of one million or the fraction of one in a million.
entries.definitionCN: 标出第一百万位、或表示百万分之一的序数形式。

entries.definition: A span of a thousand years, built from the Latin words for thousand and year.
entries.definitionCN: 一千年的时间，由拉丁语表示「千」和「年」的词构成。

entries.definition: The prefix of a thousandth, cut down from the same Latin numeral.
entries.definitionCN: 表示千分之一的前缀，由同一个拉丁数词缩减而来。

entries.definition: The number ten hundred, the step just below a million on the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 十个一百，同一数轴上紧挨在百万之下的那一级。

entries.definition: A thousand million, the step just above on the same counting scale.
entries.definitionCN: 十亿，同一计数尺度上紧挨在上的那一级。

entries.definition: A million million, a number that dwarfs a million in the same way a million dwarfs a thousand.
entries.definitionCN: 万亿，它压过百万的方式，正像百万压过千。

entries.definition: The smallest of the round large numbers, the first step of the same ladder.
entries.definitionCN: 整百数里最小的一级，同一架梯子的第一档。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin thousand wearing an Italian augmentative suffix, and its family keeps climbing the same numerical ladder in bigger steps.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个披着意大利语增大后缀的拉丁语「千」，同族词反复在同一架数字梯子上迈更大的步子。

normal.en: Mille is Latin for a thousand, and the Italian suffix -one made it a big thousand before English borrowed the word.
normal.cn: mille 是拉丁语的「千」，意大利语后缀 -one 把它变成「大一号的千」，英语才借过来。

normal.en: The plural millia is why English can say millions, a word for an uncountable crowd as much as for a number.
normal.cn: 复数 millia 是英语能说 millions 的由来，这个词既指数不清的人群，也指一个数。

normal.en: Millionaire adds -aire, the French ending for a person, directly to the fortune itself.
normal.cn: millionaire 把法语里表示人的后缀 -aire 直接加在那笔财产后面。

normal.en: Millionth adds -th, the same ending that turns four into fourth, so the ordinal is ordinary English building, not a new root.
normal.cn: millionth 加的是把 four 变成 fourth 的那个 -th，属于寻常的英语构词，不是新词根。

normal.en: One in a million works because the number is already the edge of the imaginable, so a single case inside it feels miraculous.
normal.cn: one in a million 之所以成立，是因为这个数已到想象的边缘，混在其中的单独一个便显得像奇迹。

abstract.en: A word for a sum nobody can count to is also the word for a crowd nobody can count and a fortune nobody can spend.
abstract.cn: 一个谁也数不到的数目，同时也指谁也数不清的人群和谁也花不完的财产。

abstract.en: The same six zeros can mean a packed stadium or a private bank account, depending only on who is speaking.
abstract.cn: 同样的六个零，可以是满座的体育场，也可以是私人的银行账户，区别只在于说话的是谁。

abstract.en: Million is a measuring stick that people keep using to measure hope, so it never stays a pure number for long.
abstract.cn: million 是一把人们不断拿来量希望的尺子，所以它从不久久地停留为一个纯数字。

examples.en: The archive holds a million pages of weather records.
examples.cn: 这座档案馆存有一百万页气象记录。

examples.en: Millions of birds cross this coast every autumn.
examples.cn: 每年秋天都有数以百万计的鸟飞越这片海岸。

examples.en: A million dollars would not buy that view.
examples.cn: 一百万美元也买不到那片景色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米连」——把米粒一粒粒连起来，数到一百万也数不完；记住 million 是百万。

root: 拉丁语 mille（千）的中性复数 millia 提供样式，意大利语加增大后缀 -one 造出 milioni，经古法语 million 于十五世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The exact number is the base; from it the word opens into a crowd past counting and then into the money such a number can name.
sensesIntro.cn: 精确的数目是底座；由此向外分出数不清的人群，再分出这个数目所能代表的那笔钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bid board climbing until it stops at a row of zeros nobody dares to read aloud.
core.cn: 核心意象：拍卖牌一路往上翻，最后停在一串没人敢念出声的零。

branches.en: a stadium scoreboard reading one followed by six zeros
branches.cn: 体育场记分牌上的一后跟六个零

branches.en: a queue stretching past the last visible bend in the road
branches.cn: 队伍长到看不见最后一个拐弯

branches.en: a sky so full of birds that counting stops
branches.cn: 天空满到放弃计数的鸟群

branches.en: a shipping fortune given away in small cheques
branches.cn: 一笔航运财产被一张张小额支票捐了出去

branches.en: a phrase that means both a crowd and a bank balance
branches.cn: 同一个说法既指人群，也指银行余额

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin numeral, its plural, an Italian suffix of enlargement, the French form and English endings that build a person, an ordinal and a larger scale.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁数词、它的复数、一个意大利语的增大后缀、法语形式，以及构成「人」「序数」与更大尺度的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the numeral for a thousand and its plural, the two forms from which the Italian coinage and the whole scale were built.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示「千」的数词及其复数，意大利语的造词和整条数轴都从这两个形式立起。

definition_en: the height of a place above sea level, height in general, or the perpendicular height of a geometric figure
core_image: 飞机舷窗外的雪山，仪表盘上标着飞行高度
scene: 飞机爬升到巡航高度后，窗外的河流变成了一条细线。 The plane reached a cruising altitude of ten thousand metres.
sceneCN: 这里 altitude 是「高度」（第 2 个义项：物体离地面的垂直距离）；句意是飞机达到了一万米的巡航高度。

derivatives.zh: 名词：高原，与 altitude 同源于「高」
名词：中音；高音，源自拉丁语「高」

senses.title: Height above sea level
senses.definition: the vertical distance of a place above the level of the sea, used in geography and travel
senses.definitionCN: 某地高出海平面的垂直距离，用于地理与旅行
senses.example: The village sits at an altitude of three thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄位于海拔三千米处。
senses.why: Latin altitudo came from altus, 'high', and in geography the word was fixed to the one reference line that matters, the sea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 altitudo 来自 altus「高的」，在地理中这个词被固定到唯一重要的基准线，也就是海平面。

senses.title: Height above the ground
senses.definition: the height of an aircraft or object above the ground or a chosen level at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 飞机或物体在某一时刻离地面或某一基准的高度
senses.example: The plane reached a cruising altitude of ten thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机达到了一万米的巡航高度。
senses.why: Once the word meant height in general, aviation could use it for a changing measurement rather than a fixed spot on the map.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本泛指高度，航空便用它表示不断变化的测量值，而不是地图上固定的地点。

senses.title: Perpendicular height of a figure
senses.definition: the line drawn at right angles from a vertex to the opposite side of a triangle or solid
senses.definitionCN: 从顶点垂直画到对边的线段，用于三角形或立体图形
senses.example: The area of a triangle is half the base times the altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形的面积等于底乘高的一半。
senses.why: Geometry kept the pure sense of 'height' and gave it a precise meaning: the perpendicular distance from a vertex to the opposite side.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了「高度」的纯粹含义，并给它精确定义：从顶点到对边的垂直距离。

intro.en: Altitude descends from the Latin word for height and was later borrowed by geography, aviation, and geometry.
intro.cn: altitude 源自拉丁语表示「高度」的词，后来被地理、航空与几何分别借用。

items.en: altus meant 'high, deep', and it also underlies alto and altimeter.
items.cn: altus 意为「高的、深的」，也是 alto 与 altimeter 的来源。

items.en: altitudo was the abstract noun for height or depth.
items.cn: altitudo 是表示高度或深度的抽象名词。

items.en: French passed the word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Mapmakers fixed altitude to height above sea level.
items.cn: 地图绘制者把 altitude 固定为高出海平面的高度。

items.en: Flight added the sense of an aircraft's height at a given moment.
items.cn: 航空又增添了飞机在某一时刻的高度的含义。

items.en: Mathematicians used altitude for the perpendicular height of a figure.
items.cn: 数学家用 altitude 指图形的垂直高。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one syllable; the near-meaning group separates height and elevation.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音节；近义组区分高度与海拔。

normalIntro.en: Altus is Latin for high, so altitude is the state of being high.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁 altus 意为「高」，altitude 就是「高」的状态。

normal.en: Altitude, latitude, longitude: three measurements of place.
normal.cn: altitude、latitude、longitude：三种定位的度量。

normal.en: Altitude is vertical; latitude and longitude run across the globe.
normal.cn: altitude 是垂直的，纬度和经度则铺在地球表面。

normal.en: Attitude differs by one letter and means a mindset.
normal.cn: attitude 只差一个字母，意思是心态。

normal.en: Altitude sickness strikes when the air thins.
normal.cn: 空气变稀薄时会发生高原反应。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AL-ti-tude.

abstract.en: Picture a plane window with mountains far below.
abstract.cn: 想象飞机舷窗外远处的雪山。

abstract.en: See a map marking metres above the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上标注的海拔米数。

abstract.en: Draw a perpendicular line inside a triangle.
abstract.cn: 想象在三角形里画一条垂线。

examples.en: Breathing becomes difficult at this altitude.
examples.cn: 在这个海拔上呼吸会变得困难。

examples.en: The pilot climbed to a safer altitude before turning.
examples.cn: 飞行员在转向之前爬升到更安全的高度。

examples.en: In an equilateral triangle the three altitudes meet at one point.
examples.cn: 在等边三角形中，三条高交于一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: alti 让人想到 altus「高」，-tude 是状态后缀：高的状态，就是海拔与高度。

root: 源自拉丁语 altus「高的」及其抽象名词 altitudo「高度」，十四世纪经法语进入英语；地理学固定为海拔，航空指飞行高度，几何指图形的垂直高。

sensesIntro.en: The general idea of height is fixed to three different baselines: the sea, the ground, and a figure's opposite side.
sensesIntro.cn: 「高度」这一总义被固定到三条不同基准：海平面、地面、图形的对边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cockpit gauge above a range of peaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：雪山之上驾驶舱里的高度表。

definition_en: a formal document granting rights, a written set of rules for an organization, or to hire a vehicle for private use
core_image: 一张盖着印章、写明权利的羊皮纸
scene: 小镇的档案馆里锁着一份古老文件。 The town received its charter in the Middle Ages.
sceneCN: 这里 charter 指「特许状；宪章」（第 1 个义项：授予权利的正式文件）；句意是这座小镇在中世纪获得了特许状。

senses.title: A document granting rights
senses.definition: a formal document that gives rights or privileges to a group or place
senses.definitionCN: 授予某团体或某地权利与特权的正式文件
senses.example: The town received its charter in the Middle Ages.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇在中世纪获得了特许状。
senses.why: A small sheet of paper bearing a seal was enough to grant a town its freedoms.
senses.whyCN: 一张盖印的小纸片，就足以授予一座城镇自由。

senses.title: To hire a vehicle privately
senses.definition: to hire a plane, boat or bus for private use
senses.definitionCN: 为私人用途租用飞机、船只或客车
senses.example: They chartered a boat for the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们包了一艘船度过下午。
senses.why: The paper that granted a right became the written contract that granted the use of a vessel.
senses.whyCN: 授予权利的纸，变成了授予船只使用权的书面合同。

senses.title: The rules of an organization
senses.definition: a written statement of the aims and rules of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 说明某组织宗旨与规则的书面文件
senses.example: The club revised its charter last year.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部去年修订了章程。
senses.why: An organization's founding document borrowed the name of the town's founding grant.
senses.whyCN: 组织的创立文件借用了城镇创立特许状的名称。

intro.en: Charter comes from the same Latin paper word as chart, through a small sheet that carried a grant.
intro.cn: charter 与 chart 同出拉丁语「纸」一词，经由承载授权的纸页而来。

items.en: Carta meant paper or a written document.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carta 意为纸或书面文件。

items.en: Chartula was a small sheet used for a legal grant.

items.en: English charter meant a written grant of privileges.

senses.title: A cutting tool
senses.definition: a tool with a heavy metal blade on a handle, used for cutting wood
senses.definitionCN: 带木柄的重刃工具，用来劈砍木材
senses.example: He split the log with a sharp ax.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一把锋利的斧头劈开了那截木头。
senses.why: Ax is an old Germanic word for a bladed tool, and the spelling without e is the usual American form.
senses.whyCN: ax 是日耳曼语中表示带刃工具的老词，不带 e 的拼写是常见的美式写法。

senses.title: To cut greatly
senses.definition: to reduce costs, jobs or services by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 大量削减开支、岗位或服务
senses.example: The company axed two hundred jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 公司砍掉了两百个岗位。
senses.why: Cutting wood with an ax is a vivid image for cutting a budget or a staff list, so the tool became a verb of sharp reduction.
senses.whyCN: 用斧头砍木头很适合比喻砍预算或砍人员名单，于是工具名变成了表示大幅削减的动词。

senses.title: To dismiss or cancel
senses.definition: to remove someone or end something suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然去掉某人或终止某事
senses.example: The show was axed after one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节目播了一季就被砍掉了。
senses.why: If a plan or programme is chopped off like a branch, it is ended, which is why ax also means cancelling.
senses.whyCN: 计划或节目像树枝一样被砍掉，就是被终止，所以 ax 也指取消。
